unitTitle: I'd Like a Plate of Noodles
title: Vocabulary & Language
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah memiliki pengetahuan dasar untuk menyebutkan nama makanan dan minuman yang mereka sukai dengan sederhana.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 64-66
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will learn new words about food and drinks and the containers or portions they come in (a plate of noodles, a cup of coffee, a bowl of soup, etc.).
Learners will be able to understand, identify, and say key vocabulary about food and drinks.
Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about which foods and drinks they would like, using the polite request ‘would like’.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
Ask a quick food question to set the mood, e.g. “What did you have for breakfast this morning?”
Play the letter game with a food twist. The teacher writes his/her name on the board and says a food or drink that starts with the same letter (e.g. Susan – soup).
Ask the students whose names start with that letter to stand up, say their name and a food or drink starting with the same letter (e.g. Nina – noodles). Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives: hot potato and throw the ball, where the student holding the ball says one food or drink in English.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 64.

Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to talk about what they can see in the pictures (friends laughing, a server bringing food, a cup of tea, a bowl of soup). Ask them to write any English words they know about food and restaurants in their notebooks.
Elicit some ideas from the groups and write down any key words on the board.

Read the questions together and model your own answers, e.g. “My favorite food is fried rice.”, “Some foods are spicy.”, “We can show respect by saying ‘Please’ and ‘Thank you.’” Tell students they have 5-6 minutes to discuss the questions. Encourage them to use English, but it’s acceptable to use some words in their first language.

After 5-6 minutes, stop the task and elicit some ideas from students. Tell them not to worry if the questions felt difficult, because by the end of Unit 8 they will be able to answer them more easily.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 65 and ask the class, “What can you see on the page?”
Tell students that they will do a listening task. They need to listen and write the number in each box according to the order they hear the words in the audio.

Before playing the audio, read all of the phrases together: a basket of fruit, a plate of noodles, a glass of iced tea, a cup of coffee, a serving of fries, a bowl of fried rice, pieces of grilled chicken, a bowl of soup. Point out the container words (basket, plate, glass, cup, serving, bowl, pieces).
Play audio 8.1. If needed, pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner, then play the audio again.
Check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the sentences from the audio script aloud, in pairs (e.g. “My dad drinks a cup of coffee in the morning before he goes to work.”).
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the phrases they hear.
Play audio 8.2 and encourage students to repeat the phrases loudly, and to copy the intonation they hear in the audio. Pay attention to the weak “of” in phrases like “a plate of noodles”.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
Ask students to look in their books at the Vocabulary C task and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do (1. coffee).
Put students in pairs and ask them to complete the task in around 6-8 minutes, using the food and drink words from Vocabulary A.
Then, check the answers. Write the answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the completed sentences aloud to each other, in pairs.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 58 to review the invitation language from Unit 7: ‘Would you like …?’, ‘Let’s …’, and ‘How about …?’
Put students in pairs and ask them to write invitations (questions) and responses (answers) that use the new food and drink vocabulary from page 65.
Write the following examples on the board and read them aloud together as a class:
Q: Would you like to share a serving of fries with me?
A: Yes, I would. Let’s go to the mall and share a serving of fries.
Q: How about we buy a basket of fruit for our teacher?
A: Yes, that’s a great idea because it’s her birthday today.
Give students about 6-8 minutes to write their own questions and answers, then ask them to practice giving and responding to the invitations aloud.
Elicit some questions and answers from the class, write good examples on the board, and drill them together.
Ask students to open their Student Book to page 66.

First, the teacher reads the Q&A models in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear: “What would you like to eat?” – “I would like a plate of noodles, please.” / “What would you like to drink?” – “I’d like a glass of iced tea, please.”
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the Q&A models aloud as a class.
Then, the teacher asks students to read the Q&A models together in pairs (Read with a friend).

This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs. Encourage students to change the key vocabulary in the questions and answers, using the food and drink phrases from page 65.

Explain that ‘would like’ is a polite way to say what you want and is more polite than ‘I want …’. Highlight common mistakes: “I want a soup.” → “I would like a bowl of soup, please.”; “a plate of coffee” → “a cup of coffee”; “I would like to a bowl of noodles.” → “I would like a bowl of noodles.”
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at the practice task B on Student Book page 66 and ask, “What can you see in pictures 1-5?”
Read the questions together aloud as a class, then read the example (number 1) together: “I would like a glass of iced tea, please.”
Put students in pairs and ask them to write what each person or group of people would like to eat or drink. Remind them to use ‘We would (We’d) like …’ for groups, and to always add ‘please’.
Ask students to check their answers with a new partner, then elicit answers from the class and write them on the board.
Ask students to take turns reading the questions and answers aloud together. Student A asks the questions first and Student B answers them, then they swap roles.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Ask students to create their ‘Perfect Menu’: “If you could eat and drink whatever you want for a whole day, what would you choose?”
Show the ‘My Perfect Menu’ template on the screen or draw it on the board: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, and Snacks, each with a Food and a Drink line.
Reinforce that they should use the phrase ‘I would like …’ for each sentence, e.g. “Breakfast – Food: I would like a bowl of fried rice. Drink: I would like a glass of orange juice.”
Give students about 10 minutes to complete the menu.
Then, put students into groups of three or four. Each student shows their menu and says what they would like to eat and drink.
Ask each group to decide which person has the best (most perfect) menu, and ask one person from each group to present it to the class.
Choose 1-2 students to order their favorite meal politely, using the container words and ‘I’d like …, please.’ (e.g. “I’d like a plate of noodles and a glass of iced tea, please.”)
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: pengamatan pelafalan saat drill kosakata (listen and repeat).
Pemeriksaan jawaban latihan kosakata dan language practice di Student Book.
Unjuk kerja lisan: peserta didik memakai kosakata & struktur baru dalam kalimat sendiri.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?

Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
